Say how each cell is made from the statistics

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_cells.Rd

plan_cells() gives the cell templates: the text a cell prints, written with the statistics' names in braces ("{mean} ({sd})", "{n} ({p:%})"). It is usually the first verb after table_plan(), since it decides what the rows of a block are; plan_digits() then fills in the decimals the templates leave open. It also takes the settings of how cells are made — a row per statistic instead of a template, which number a token reads, what an empty cell prints — as widen_ard() takes them.

Usage

plan_cells(.plan, ..., stats = NULL, value = NULL, na = NULL, notes = NULL)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan(). The pipe passes it by position; the dot keeps a name in ... such as p (cards' percentage) from being taken for it.

...

The templates, as widen_ard(cells = ) takes them: one bare entry for every cell, or entries named by what they apply to. Each entry is a template, a named vector of templates (one row each, the names the rows' labels), guards (c(n == 0 ~ "0", "{n} ({p})")) or cell_rows(). The names, from the most specific:

<variable>

an analysis variable, AGE = "{mean} ({sd})".

<stat group>

a group of plan_stat_groups(), orr_ci = cell_rows(...).

<context>

an ARD context, tabulate = "{n}".

continuous, categorical

a kind of variable.

default

everything else (the unnamed entry).

In a table of plan_stat_groups(), a record of a split variable (.variables) takes its variable's entry, else its group's, before its context or kind; a record that went whole to .others takes its variable's, then its context's or kind's, its group's only after them. The names of the arguments after ... are reserved: a variable called stats, value, na or notes cannot be keyed here; name it otherwise in the ARD.

A later call replaces a key's entry as a whole, a named vector of templates too: its rows are not merged with the earlier call's.

An unnamed vector of several templates, c("{n} ({p})", "{n}"), is one row: the first template whose statistics the record has wins, as with guards. A template with no token prints as written, so a constant cell is text ("-", and "" an empty cell). A list holds the same things (list(n = "{N}", Mean = "{mean}") is the named vector). Anything else — NULL, NA, a number, TRUE, a factor, character(0), a template that is NA — stops at the verb, naming the key.

stats

"cells" (default) fills a template per cell; "rows" makes each statistic a row of its own (no template).

value

With stats = "rows": the raw number ("stat") or cards' formatted text ("stat_fmt") in each row. With templates an open {x} takes stat_fmt when the ARD has it and stat otherwise, and {x:stat_fmt} / {x:.1f} say so per token.

na

What fills a cell no template could (a statistic the ARD does not have). On a plan of a table that is already built (no statistics), na alone is taken: as_rtftables()'s na, what a missing value prints as.

notes

FALSE stops the message listing the statistics no template used; TRUE (or NULL, the default) reports them.

Value

The plan, with one more layer. The settings hold however the plan is run, by plan_apply() or by rtf_tables(doc, plan).

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; widen_ard() for the template language.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

# Invented summary statistics, one row a statistic (no cards needed)
st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 7),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "AGE", "AGE", "SEX", "SEX", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, NA, NA, "F", "F", "M", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c(rep("continuous", 3), rep("categorical", 4)), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "sd", "median", "n", "p", "n", "p"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.2, 9.81, 60, 12, 0.6, 8, 0.4,
                63.5, 10.2, NA, 20, 1, 0, 0))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable"))

# Minimal: one template per kind, the digits written in the template;
# the name of a continuous template is its row's label
p |>
  plan_cells(continuous  = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})"),
             categorical = "{n} ({p:.1f%})", notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_apply("table")
#>   group     label     Placebo       Active
#> 1   AGE Mean (SD) 61.2 (9.81) 63.5 (10.20)
#> 2   SEX         F   12 (60.0)   20 (100.0)
#> 3   SEX         M    8 (40.0)      0 (0.0)

# A demographics block: AGE as two named rows, a zero count printed
# as "0" rather than "0 (0.0)", and a median the ARD lacks as "-"
p |>
  plan_cells(continuous  = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
                             "Median"    = "{median:.1f}"),
             categorical = c(n == 0 ~ "0", "{n} ({p:.1f%})"),
             na = "-") |>
  plan_apply("table")
#>   group     label     Placebo       Active
#> 1   AGE Mean (SD) 61.2 (9.81) 63.5 (10.20)
#> 2   AGE    Median        60.0            -
#> 3   SEX         F   12 (60.0)   20 (100.0)
#> 4   SEX         M    8 (40.0)            0
